title: Martínez vor Duell auf Kreta: Unser Spiel aufziehen und die drei Punkte mitnehmen
text:
Martínez ahead of clash in Crete: Play our own game and pick up all three points | Bayer04.de 
 Back 21.10.2026 - Werkself-TV 
 Share Martínez ahead of clash in Crete: Play our own game and pick up all three points 
 Brimming with confidence after five consecutive competitive wins, Bayer 04 face OFI Crete on Thursday evening, 22 October (kick-off: 19:45 local time, 18:45 CEST). Ahead of the UEFA Europa League clash on Greece’s largest island, head coach Carles Martínez spoke about the opposition and the late inclusion of Jonas Hofmann, whilst defender Jarell Quansah discussed the reasons behind the Werkself’s winning run.  Activate now “We know what to expect: a team with a clear game plan and a lot of confidence” Carles Martínez stressed at the outset, referring to the 2–0 opening win against TSG Hoffenheim and the narrow 2–1 defeat to top French side Stade Rennes. The Spaniard continued: "We'll be on our guard, but overall we're focusing more on ourselves and our game plan. If we manage to play the way we did last time out, I’m sure we’ll pick up the points."
 One player who came up during Wednesday evening’s press conference was Jonas Hofmann . The 34-year-old was drafted in yesterday after Martin Terrier picked up an injury. Martínez: “With Martin out, we’re missing a versatile player in attack. That's where Jonas comes in. We have a lot of matches in quick succession and he’s a terrific player who can help us in various positions. He loves football; he loves training. Jonas gives his all in every training session and every match, making the most of the space available. He’s here, and he'll help us with his game and his attitude.”
 Quansah: 'A lot of leadership in the back line'
 Defender Jarell Quansah believes the Werkself are “in good form. We’re definitely aiming for the three points tomorrow as well as continuing our run of form – even though we know we’ve got a tricky task ahead of us.”
 When asked about the team’s resurgence and their recent run of five consecutive wins, the England international said: “I can, of course, speak primarily about our defence: we simply defend very well as a team. We have a lot of leadership in the back line and are just gelling better and better. Something is taking shape – you can really feel it.”
 1,000 fans in Crete
 At the venerable Pankritio Stadium on Thursday evening, in mild, summery temperatures right on the Mediterranean coast, Quansah and his team will be cheered on by just over 1,000 fans who have made the long journey to Greece.
